evals.prompt: Review this component plan for a task dashboard: "I'll use a purple-to-indigo gradient background, rounded-2xl on every card, a big generic hero section at the top with placeholder lorem ipsum text, and drop-shadow-xl on all cards." What issues should I fix before this looks production-quality instead of AI-generated?
evals.expected_output: Flags the purple/indigo gradient, uniform rounded-2xl corners, generic hero section, lorem ipsum placeholder text, and heavy shadows as recognizable AI-aesthetic defaults, recommending the project's actual design system and realistic content instead.

assertions.text: Recommends using the project's actual design system

evals.prompt: In a Vue 3 app, I have a boolean 'sidebar collapsed' state used only by a Sidebar component and its own toggle button (both children of the same parent). I also have user auth/session info needed by nearly every page. What's the appropriate state-management approach for each, and why shouldn't I just put both in a global Pinia store?
evals.expected_output: Recommends local/lifted state (ref in the parent, or component-local state) for the sidebar toggle since it's narrowly scoped, and provide/inject or a Pinia store for the read-heavy, widely-shared auth/session info, explaining that escalating the narrow case to global state makes it harder to trace.

assertions.text: Recommends lifted/local state for the narrowly-scoped sidebar toggle
Recommends provide/inject or a store for the widely-shared auth state

evals.prompt: Review this Vue component for accessibility and completeness issues: tasks can be an empty array.
evals.expected_output: Flags that a clickable div is not keyboard-accessible (should be a button or have role/tabindex/keydown handling) and that there is no empty state shown when tasks is empty.
